verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. The formula is the paper's under α↔n, ν↔r: radialDivisor r n = (n+1)(n+r), and the Lean n-th coefficient inputJet I ε A n 0 η is F_α(η) (profile = Σ Yⁿ · inputJet A n 0 η, no factorial normalisation). Rewriting: the two Lean theorems carry an extra index m, the order of the η-derivative; m = 0 is (B.5) verbatim, larger m is its η-derivative, which the paper's identity of functions of η gives at once. The definitional direction is reversed: Lean takes (B.5) as the definition of J_ν (inverseScale/inverseData, and the raw-coefficient regularInverseJet) and proves the paper's defining properties afterwards — the ODE Y G_YY + ν G_Y = F in regularInverse_actual_equation and G(0)=0 in AxisEvaluationAlgebra.regularInverse_axis_zero (line 148) — whereas the paper defines J_ν by the ODE and states (B.5) as a consequence. Lean's hypothesis is 1 ≤ r, more general than the paper's ν ∈ {1,2}.
